title: Trace Fingerprinting & Slack Actionable Incident Bundles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Incident responders often need a condensed, actionable context bundle (trace snippet, top error metrics, and a pointer to a focused runbook) surfaced directly in PagerDuty and Slack to reduce time-to-identify and time-to-restore. Current PD/Slack alerts contain only summary and links; responders must manually navigate traces and dashboards.

Goal: Implement a service-agnostic enrichment pipeline that: (1) computes a deterministic trace fingerprint at span-ingest time, (2) extracts a minimal trace snippet (top spans, error stack, heuristic root-cause markers), (3) correlates recent error/latency metrics and representative logs, and (4) composes an actionable attachment delivered to PagerDuty incidents and Slack alerts with one-click runbook links and incident-creation metadata. Also seed a postmortem skeleton when critical incidents are acknowledged.

Non-goals: full-text tracing viewer in PD/Slack; replacing the Console trace UX. We will not store full traces long-term in the enrichment store (only snippets + reference keys).
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment pipeline produces a trace fingerprint and snippet for >=90% of critical incidents in staging during a 72h smoke run
PagerDuty incidents created from the enrichment pipeline include a JSON attachment with: fingerprint, top-3 spans, error message summary, top metric shards, and a link to the Console trace + runbook
Slack alert blocks display condensed snippet, severity tag, one-click runbook link, and 'Create Postmortem' button that seeds the skeleton document in Confluence
End-to-end added latency to hot request paths is <5ms P95 (we implement async ingestion; blocking calls are disallowed)
Sampling and rate-limiting prevents more than 2 enrichment writes/sec per service by default
Automated tests and chaos scenario validate fallbacks when traces are missing (e.g., attach metrics-only bundle)
Security review completed: no sensitive fields (PII/headers) included in attachments; KMS used for any stored sensitive metadata
Operational dashboards show enrichment success rate, attach latency, and storage usage; alerted when enrichment failure rate >5% for 1 hour
tasks: Design schema for trace fingerprint and snippet (fields, TTL, privacy redaction rules)
Add lightweight fingerprinting hook to span-ingest pipeline (async exporter to enrichment topic)
Build enrichment worker service: correlator that glues traces, metrics, and logs, and emits PD/Slack payloads
Implement PagerDuty attachment composer and Slack Block Kit generator with interactive actions
Create runbook templater and postmortem skeleton seeder (Confluence API integration)
Implement feature flag and rollout plan (staging -> canary -> org-wide) with kill switch
Write e2e tests that simulate high-error bursts, missing traces, and long-tail latency to verify behavior
Load test enrichment worker at peak alerting rates and validate backpressure behavior
Security review & threat model with Security team (KMS, PII scanning, least-privilege API tokens)
Monitor and dashboard: create Grafana panels for enrichment success, PD attach latency, Slack failures
comments: 2025-02-13 Maya Chen: Created ticket after post-incident retro for INC-2025-01; linked to observability roadmap. Initial hypothesis: responders waste ~8-12 minutes per incident when manual trace hunting required.

2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Architecture spike completed. Chose async fingerprinting in the span-ingest exporter to avoid adding tail latency. Prototype published: github.com/redwood/infr/trace-fingerprint-proto PR #1472.

2025-02-20 Design review (Lara Patel): Recommended Slack block affordances and compact runbook CTA. Suggested limiting message size to 4KB to avoid Slack truncation. Action: update composer to prioritize top-3 spans + error summary.

2025-02-24 Security review (Jasmine R.): Raised concern about stack snippets containing user PII. Decision: redact query params and any header values; use regex-based scrubbers and a configurable allowlist. Added security_review_required=true on ticket.
2025-02-26 Engineering note (Liam): Implemented fallback behavior: if no trace snippet available, attach top-k metric slices and an aggregated log sample. Tested in dev with synthetic events.

2025-03-01 QA (Rohit Mehra): Staging run results: enrichment success 92% over 48h. Two failure modes observed: (1) enrichment worker OOM when concurrent alerts spike; (2) PagerDuty API rate-limited on bursts. Mitigations: increase worker memory, add retry/backoff plus PD rate-adapter queueing.

2025-03-03 Maya Chen (PM): Approved cutover plan for canary. Requirements: monitor enrich_fail_rate, pd_rate_limit, and slack_block_errors, and auto-rollback if enrich_fail_rate >8% sustained for 15m.

Notes: Linked docs -> Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Trace+Fingerprinting+Enrichment; GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood/infr/pull/1472, https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/688; Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/obs/enrichment-overview
decision_log: Synchronous vs Async: Async chosen to preserve request path latency; fingerprinting done in exporter with message to enrichment topic
Storage TTL: snippets stored for 21 days by default to balance investigation usefulness vs storage costs
Sampling policy: default 1:1 for P0/P1 alerts, adaptive 1:10 for noisy services; configurable per-service
Privacy: use scrubber pipeline and deny-list; security team will run weekly audits
next_steps: Finish PD attachment composer and wire to enrichment worker (target 2025-03-10)
Complete Confluence postmortem template integration and QA the 'Create Postmortem' button (target 2025-03-12)
Run canary across two low-risk services; monitor metrics and PD/Slack API error surface (target 2025-03-14)
Prepare runbook for SRE on rollback and hit-zero thresholds before org-wide rollout
